action_summary: The standing question's verdict-level answers hold (audit, ONE_TRY, THE_PRIOR, TWO_DOORS); what a 'learned it on the first try' claim needs underneath is an acceptance gate that can only pass when it actually ran the project's tests. This round measures that gate. The project-test baseline in canonical/swe_kernel/egraph_and_deductive_synthesizer_v1.py has three suite sites (_collect_project_bad_tests, _verify_no_new_test_failures, _run_project_tests) and all three inherited _run_cmd's implicit 20.0 s helper default. Two failure modes measured on 8439f609: (M1) a 21 s unittest.TestCase fixture died at 20.3 s with PROJECT_TEST_BASELINE_UNMEASURABLE while still running -- the suite was runnable, the gate quit; the brain's own canonical/tests did not finish in 300 s either (rc=-9 at 300.3 s, SUBSTRATE_CAVEAT), so the budget must be an explicit reviewed number, not a helper default. (M2, the dangerous one) a pytest-shaped test file (bare def test_it, no TestCase class) loads as ZERO tests under Python 3.11's unittest loader (loader.py:120-124 collects TestCase subclasses only), the probe printed an empty bad-list in 0.0 s, and the gate read that as 'no failures' -- an empty measurement sold as green; the extract-constant door showcase had been PASSing on exactly this vacuous baseline. The fix ships three changes in one file: BASELINE_BUDGET_S=300.0 passed explicitly at all three sites; suite children exit 3 with BASELINE_NO_DISCOVERABLE_TESTS when countTestCases()==0, which the parent converts into the named refusal PROJECT_TEST_BASELINE_UNMEASURABLE:TEST_FILES_FOUND_NONE_DISCOVERABLE (door status FAIL_CLOSED__CAPABILITY_REFUSED_TEST_FILES_FOUND_NONE_DISCOVERABLE) only when test files exist inside discovery's own scope; and _test_files_present mirrors the loader's traversal (direct test*.py/_test.py files, descend only into __init__.py packages) instead of an rglob -- the first rglob draft was caught by test_three_pillar (tests under a non-package directory discover never descends) and replaced before commit. After: the 21 s suite measures in 21.0 s; function-style files refuse by name at both sites; empty and out-of-scope projects proceed exactly as base; a spy over the three sites shows [300.0, 300.0, 300.0]; the extract chain passes end to end against a MEASURED TestCase suite (PASS__RAW_GOAL_EXECUTED_AND_EXACT_SEMANTIC_ACCEPTANCE_VERIFIED, python.swe.transform_and_synthesize.v1, EXTRACTED_CONSTANT=7) and the same sentence over a function-style suite now refuses. Regression ledger: 6 new pins in test_the_gate_waits_for_the_suite_it_measures_v1 (including the 21 s measurement and the door showcase); contracts 49/49, three_pillar+contracts 52/52, door/refactor/near-miss batch 36 passed 1 skipped; substrate restored by scripts/restore_substrate_v1.py (SUBSTRATE_READY 10/10); test_hardcore memoize failure stash-verified pre-existing on base (OUTPUT_ALREADY_EXISTS), not fixed silently. Next instrument named, not smuggled: a pytest fallback when importable, its own measured round; >300 s suites still refuse fail-closed.
explicit_user_authorization: Owner directive 2026-11-12: determine what is real about instant learning and advanced coding/computer-use actions, kill bad ideas before implementation, think from first principles, maximize use of the latest research, and always push and merge completed work. This change is the acceptance-gate half of that standing order: the gate that decides whether a change is 'accepted' was measured and found to have two non-measuring modes (quit at 20 s; pass on an empty measurement). Fixing it is a zero-spend runtime repair with pins, not a governance change, no sentience claim.

2. Raise _run_cmd's global default -- rejected: the helper serves mypy and import checks where 20 s is right; only the suite sites needed the budget
3. Pytest fallback in this round -- deferred by name: needs its own measured exit-code map and output parsing, not a smuggled edit
4. Drop the file-existence condition (refuse any zero count) -- rejected: would break empty projects and out-of-scope targets, caught by the three_pillar control
obs_solution.losing_routes_reason: The global-default raise over-waits everywhere else; the unconditional refusal breaks empty projects; the pytest fallback without a measured parsing contract is exactly the kind of under-tested gate change this round is fixing. Only the scoped budget-plus-named-refusal survives the measurements and the controls.
